questions.title: How exactly does the entropy‑based patching algorithm decide where to cut a byte sequence?
questions.question_body: The paper describes two variant constraints for entropy patching: a global threshold $\theta_g$ and an approximate monotonicity constraint $\theta_r$. I am unclear on how these are applied in practice. For a given byte $x_t$, do we compute its entropy $H(x_t)$ using the small LM and then compare it to $\theta_g$ *and* the difference $H(x_t)-H(x_{t-1})$ to $\theta_r$?  Is the global constraint applied first, and only if it fails we look at the monotonic constraint, or are they combined with an OR/AND logic?  Also, how is the threshold $\theta_g$ chosen to obtain a target average patch size?

questions.title: Why does the paper claim that BPE tokenizers cannot satisfy the incremental patching property?
questions.question_body: In Section 2.5 the authors define incremental patching as $f_p(\mathbf{x}_{<i}) = f_p(\mathbf{x})_{<i}$ and say BPE violates this because the same prefix can be tokenized differently depending on future bytes. Could someone give a concrete example with a short string that shows this behavior? Additionally, is there a known modification (e.g., using a delimiter token) that makes BPE incremental, and what would be the trade‑offs of such a modification?

questions.title: What is the role of the cross‑attention layers in the local encoder and decoder, and why are they placed after each transformer layer?
questions.question_body: The architecture section mentions that after every transformer layer in the encoder (and before every transformer layer in the decoder) there is a cross‑attention block that pools bytes into patch representations (or vice‑versa). I am confused about why this repeated pooling is necessary – would a single cross‑attention at the end of the encoder be sufficient? Also, how does the query initialization (max‑pool, hash embedding, or learned) affect performance, according to the ablations?

questions.title: How are Bits‑Per‑Byte (BPB) values comparable across models with different patch sizes and vocabularies?
questions.question_body: The paper reports BPB as a tokenizer‑independent metric. However, models with larger average patches process fewer steps per byte, which could affect loss scaling. Is BPB directly comparable between a model using space‑patching (average 6 bytes/patch) and one using entropy‑patching (average 4.5 bytes/patch)? Does the definition of BPB implicitly assume a per‑byte cross‑entropy loss that is independent of how many transformer steps were taken?

questions.title: What is the exact FLOP formula used for the latent global transformer when counting "per byte" cost?
questions.question_body: In Section 4.1 the FLOP count for BLT includes a term \text{Transf. FL}(h_{\mathcal{G}}, l_{\mathcal{G}}, m=n_{ctx}/n_p, V=0) / n_p.  I want to understand each argument: $h_{\mathcal{G}}$ hidden size, $l_{\mathcal{G}}$ layers, $m$ context length in patches (so $n_{ctx}$ bytes divided by number of patches), and $V$ = 0 because there is no output vocabulary projection at this stage. Could someone expand this into the standard QKV + FFN FLOP equations and show how it reduces to per‑byte cost? Also, why is there no addition of patch‑dependent positional embeddings?

questions.title: Why does resetting the entropy model context with newlines help avoid "entropy drift"?
questions.question_body: The authors mention that during large‑scale training they reset the entropy model context with new lines because otherwise "entropy drift" occurs when processing long repetitive sections (e.g., multiple‑choice questions). How does changing the context influence the entropy estimates? Is it simply that a smaller context prevents the small LM from over‑fitting to repeated patterns, or is there a more subtle statistical effect?

questions.title: How does BLT’s "patch size" interact with the fixed context length in bytes when comparing inference flop budgets?
questions.question_body: The experiments keep the number of bytes per batch constant while varying average patch size, which changes the number of patches processed per batch. The paper says they reduce sequence length for larger patches to keep total bytes constant. I’m unsure how this influences inference FLOPs: does a larger patch size always reduce FLOPs linearly, or are there diminishing returns due to cross‑attention overheads? Also, how is the "fixed inference scaling" experiment (Figure 5) designed to isolate this effect?

questions.title: Can BLT be trained end‑to‑end without a pre‑trained entropy model for patching?
questions.question_body: Section 3.1 says entropy patching uses a separate lightweight LM trained on the same data distribution. Have the authors tried learning a boundary predictor jointly with BLT (as in Nawrot et al., 2023)? If not, what are the main obstacles? Would an end‑to‑end differentiable boundary predictor introduce bias in patch granularity or increase training FLOPs significantly?

questions.title: What is the intuition behind "dynamic allocation of compute" when predicting first bytes of words versus later bytes?
questions.question_body: The introduction argues that predicting first characters after spaces is high entropy and thus should trigger a global transformer step, whereas later characters are low entropy and can be handled by cheap local layers. How does BLT actually implement this at inference time? Is it purely based on precomputed patch boundaries derived from entropy, or does the model decide on‑the‑fly whether to invoke the latent transformer for each byte?

questions.title: How does "byte‑ifying" a pretrained Llama 3 model work in practice?
questions.question_body: Section 7 describes initializing BLT’s global transformer with weights from Llama 3.1 and then training with a reduced learning rate for those layers while using a higher LR for encoder/decoder. I am unclear on how token embeddings from Llama 3 are transferred to Byte embeddings: Are they discarded entirely? Does initializing only the global transformer guarantee compatibility with new byte‑level inputs, or is there some mismatch between positional embeddings or output heads that needs special handling?
